free_tier.stated: Tunnel speed limit 10 Mibps; 2 tunnels; 5 GiB traffic per month; daily check-in grants free traffic. [translated]

egress.terms: 5 GiB per month on the free plan, plus whatever the daily check-in adds; the pricing page does not state the check-in amount.; ingress: udp
egress.free_allowance: 5 GiB per month on the free plan, plus whatever the daily check-in adds; the pricing page does not state the check-in amount.

interface_detail: Vendor launcher for Windows/Linux/Android/OpenWRT, or a standard frpc config; the docs publish an API token page.
tooling: vendor launcher or frpc plus wg-quick on the local side
chaining: Carries a WG handshake from a CGNAT box to a WG server on a free VM only if a UDP-enabled node is used and the 5 GiB lasts.
binding_note: 5 GiB per month is about 200 times below 1 TiB, so the byte quota fails long before the 10 Mibps shaper could matter.

identity_cost.detail: Real-name verification is mandatory: the FAQ says to buy a verification slot, enter name and ID number, then scan a QR code in the Alipay app with face check, and that it costs CNY 1. A Telegram status post dated 2024-07-09 says overseas nodes also require it from that date.

reliability_note: A Telegram status post says mainland nodes refuse to start a tunnel from a non-mainland client IP; some nodes carry a 'no UDP' marker.
confidence_note: The quota and the real-name procedure are both on vendor pages read today. Raising the rung would need a probe of an actual UDP tunnel.

evidence.proved: free plan is 10 Mibps, 2 tunnels, 5 GiB per month
real-name verification is mandatory, costs CNY 1, uses Alipay face check and an ID number
a UDP tunnel type exists with its own option set
servers can be marked 'no UDP'; the client must pick a node without that marker
'To use NetherNet you must tunnel both TCP and UDP' and the tunnel form takes 'Tunnel type: UDP' [translated]

notes: Forum roundups describe the traffic as 'claimable by daily check-in', which matches the vendor page but understates that the base allowance is 5 GiB. The overseas-node exemption claimed in the nodeloc roundup is contradicted by the vendor's own 2024-07-09 status post.

extras.wg_detail: Help docs list a UDP tunnel type with per-tunnel options (no_budp2, bandwidth_limit), and the Palworld guide says to pick the UDP tunnel type and to avoid servers marked 'no UDP'. A WG datagram fits inside that UDP tunnel; no WG conf is issued.
extras.volume_stated: 5 GiB per month on the free plan, plus whatever the daily check-in adds; the pricing page does not state the check-in amount.
extras.transit_note: SakuraFrp nodes carry the datagrams; the client's local service terminates them.
